proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:nls, eq:energy. Write \(u(t)=\Phi(t)\phi\) for the smooth solution of \[
 i\partial_tu+\Delta u=|u|^4u,\qquad u(0)=\phi.\] Use normalized Haar measure, so that \(\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^3}(1+|k|^2)|\widehat u(k)|^2\). The conserved mass and energy are \[
 M[u]=\|u\|_2^2,\qquad
 H[u]=\tfrac12\|\nabla u\|_2^2+\tfrac16\|u\|_6^6.\] Changing to unnormalized Lebesgue measure multiplies all squared norms and the calculations below by \((2\pi)^3\) and does not change the argument.

Equation reference: eq:partition. Definition A.8 on p. 44, paraphrased with its quantifiers retained, calls a finite partition \(-T=\tau_0<\cdots<\tau_m=T\) an \((A,\delta)\)-partition with respect to \(\phi\) if \(A>\delta>0\) and \[
 \|\Phi(\tau_{j-1})\phi\|_{H^1}\leq A,\qquad
 \|\Phi(t)\phi\|_{Z([\tau_{j-1},\tau_j])}<\delta
 \quad(1\leq j\leq m).\] The first bound is imposed at the existing left endpoints, not at every time. The critical \(Z\) norm is defined on p. 38. It decreases upon restriction to a subinterval. On intervals of length less than one it is a sum of two time-\(L^p\) Besov norms, with finite \(p=4.1\) and \(p=100\). Consequently, for a smooth trajectory, \(\|u\|_{Z([-T,T])}\to0\) as \(T\downarrow0\).

Kind: paraphrase

Location: Definition A.8 and Proposition A.9, PDF p44

Text: For any A>delta>0, phi in H1 and an (A,delta)-partition of [-T,T] with H1 bounds only at existing left endpoints and Z norm <delta on each interval, every refinement remains an (A,delta)-partition with the same A and delta.
